title: Large Language Models
summary: Improving the efficiency, stability, and deployability of large-scale language models through research in routing, sparsity, training dynamics, and inference optimization.
description:
The lab is built around the idea that progress in AI is not only about making models larger. It is also about making computation more useful. In practice, that means studying how to allocate compute more intelligently, reduce waste in training and inference, improve stability as systems scale, and preserve useful behavior when models are pushed into real operating conditions.

This program is the primary current focus of Neryva. It sits at the intersection of architecture research, training dynamics, and deployment engineering — the areas where efficiency, stability, and real-world constraints all matter at once.

keyQuestions.question: How should routing objectives balance throughput gains from expert specialization against the risk of training instability?
Which sparsity patterns preserve useful model behavior under deployment-time memory and latency constraints?
What early measurements can predict whether a training configuration will be stable at larger scale?
How can inference serving pipelines adapt dynamically to workload characteristics and hardware heterogeneity?
Can routing and sparsity decisions be co-optimized during training without introducing convergence problems?

currentWork: Current work is focused on literature review and problem formulation across all four technical areas. Initial experiments in routing objective design are being scoped.
